content: coffee a controlled explosion on a film set near the O2 arena in London ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and a lorry. London fire brigade said crews were called to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown shortly before eight pm on Saturday. The blaze was brought under control just over an hour later after twenty‑five firefighters attended, with no injuries reported. It is understood the fire followed a pre‑planned filming event at the site close to the capital’s O2 arena, which hosts concerts by Niall Horan and Texas next week. London fire brigade posted on X on Saturday evening, saying the fire at the open air yard in Silvertown is now under control, one van was destroyed and most of a car and lorry were damaged, and there are currently no reports of any injuries. It added that the fire in Silvertown followed a controlled explosion at a film set which spread out of control, firefighters worked quickly to extinguish it, and crews will remain on scene for the remainder of the evening. The open‑air yard in Dock Road where the fire took place is also near London’s cable car link across the River Thames. A Met police spokesperson said they are aware of reports of explosions being heard in the vicinity of the O2 in Greenwich.
